items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I asked Cecil who he was and was told that his name was Jabbo Smith

ctx.x: The band started and Charlie Johnson left the piano and I never saw him anymore that night. But what a band! it had been quite some time back when I heard Fletcher Henderson and here I was listening to an orchestra that was in the same class as Fletcher and I had never heard of the band before. There was an outstanding trumpet player who played fast, clean as a whistle and also used a derby which he waved over the bell of the horn to get an open horn wa-wa effect. I had not heard Armstrong in person and I…
I asked Cecil who he was and was told that his name was Jabbo Smith

I was overwhelmed with joy at hearing and seeing this man who to my estimation played more trumpet than all the trumpet players I had heard put together, and the band was swinging like no band I had ever heard could do.
